subject.title: feat(onboarding): unified empty-state with provider icons, websites, and recommended installs

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently curate a third-party installation catalog and expose icon and website as providerAuthChoices API, or should recommendations be derived from activatable provider/plugin-owned metadata?
rationale: The choice establishes ongoing vendor-curation policy and a public plugin contract; repository architecture guidance favors owner-plugin metadata, but accepting a core catalog is a legitimate product decision only maintainers can make.

options.title: Derive from activatable metadata
options.body: Have provider or plugin owners declare recommendation presentation and eligibility, and render only routes setup can activate or verify.

options.title: Approve the core catalog
options.body: Keep the nine-tool bundled catalog with an explicit owner, inclusion criteria, update policy, and tests preventing unusable recommendations.

options.title: Split the feature
options.body: Land the additive icon and website transport separately and defer the curated recommendation catalog until its ownership is settled.

recommendation.title: Derive from activatable metadata
recommendation.body: Have provider or plugin owners declare recommendation presentation and eligibility, and render only routes setup can activate or verify.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent onboarding work and related credential-less setup proposal make this the strongest available routing candidate for the product choice.
